input.question: Which educational institution did Károly Szakonyi attend?

documents.text:
Title: The Formative Years of Károly Szakonyi: A Hungarian Literary Icon

In the heart of Budapest, Hungary, a young Károly Szakonyi was laying the foundations for a remarkable literary career. Born in 1935, Szakonyi would go on to become one of Hungary's most celebrated writers and playwrights, leaving an indelible mark on the country's cultural landscape. But before he rose to fame, Szakonyi's educational journey began at Madách Imre High School, a prestigious institution in Budapest that played a pivotal role in shaping his artistic vision. As a teenager, Szakonyi walked through the gates of Madách Imre High School, surrounded by the imposing buildings and rich history of the institution. Founded in 1872, the school was named after Imre Madách, a renowned Hungarian poet and playwright, whose works had a profound impact on the country's literary heritage. It was here, amidst the academic rigor and cultural richness of Madách Imre High School, that Szakonyi's passion for writing began to take root. During his time at the school, Szakonyi was exposed to a wide range of literary influences, from the works of Hungarian masters like Sándor Márai and Dezső Kosztolányi to the classical plays of Shakespeare and Molière. The school's emphasis on language, literature, and drama helped Szakonyi develop his writing skills, and he soon began to experiment with his own creative voice. One of Szakonyi's earliest literary endeavors was a school newspaper, which he co-founded with his classmates. This humble publication became a platform for the young writer to express himself, sharing his thoughts on literature, politics, and social issues. The experience not only honed his writing skills but also instilled in him a sense of responsibility and discipline, essential qualities for a writer. Szakonyi's time at Madách Imre High School was also marked by his involvement in the school's drama club. Under the guidance of dedicated teachers, he participated in numerous productions, both on and off stage. This exposure to the world of theater helped Szakonyi develop his skills as a playwright, and he soon began to write his own plays, many of which would go on to be performed at the school. The evidence of Szakonyi's attendance at Madách Imre High School is well-documented.
